## Problem

Implement a single-screen mobile application in Xcode that displays a table view populated with fifty timer rows.

Each row behaves as an independent timer. While a cell is on screen, its timer should increment every 0.1 seconds. When the user taps a cell, that cell’s timer should pause or stop. As soon as a cell scrolls out of view, its timer must stop. When the same cell scrolls back into view, its timer should become active again.

In one variation of this task, a pull-down gesture starts a brand-new timer and stops the previously running timer. Tapping a row in this variation stops that specific row’s timer.

If time allows, improve the implementation for better performance or reliability.

**Additional detail:** Every cell contains a red dot.

**Requirements**

* Build a one-page app in Xcode.
* Use a table view.
* Include 50 timer rows.
* Visible cells automatically count every 0.1 seconds.
* Tapping a cell pauses or stops that cell's timer.
* A cell's timer stops when the cell leaves the visible area.
* A cell's timer activates or reactivates when the cell enters the visible area.
* Pulling down starts a new timer and stops the old timer (in the pull-down variant).
* If time permits, optimize the implementation.

**Additional Part**

* Each cell has a red dot.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Treat each row’s timer as data in a model (elapsed time + running state), not as separate UI components, so cells can be refreshed from a single source of truth.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Drive all timers with one shared timer or CADisplayLink that updates the models, then reload only visible cells to avoid creating 50 independent timers.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Watch cell reuse: always set the cell’s label from its model when configuring it, and ensure a tap toggles only the tapped row’s state, not a recycled cell’s old value.

</details>
